nodes.summary: The lineages (as blocks of sampled genes, indexed by lineage label) after the first `t` coalescence events of a history, starting from the singletons `{0}, …, {n - 1}`.
nodes.title: Lineage blocks after the first coalescence events

nodes.summary: The ancestral partitions of the sample along a history, as lists of blocks indexed by lineage label; entry `t` (for `t < n`) is the partition after `t` coalescence events.
nodes.title: Ancestral partitions along a history, indexed by lineage label

nodes.summary: The number of pairs of `k` lineages is `k.choose 2`.
nodes.title: Number of pairs of lineages

nodes.summary: `#histories * 2^{n-1} = n! (n - 1)!`, i.e. there are `n! (n - 1)! / 2^{n-1}` ranked labeled histories of `n` labeled genes (Edwards 1970).
nodes.title: Number of ranked labeled histories

nodes.summary: The unordered pairs of lineages when there are `k` lineages labeled `0, …, k - 1`.
nodes.title: Unordered pairs of lineages

nodes.summary: Merge the lineages (blocks of sampled genes) at positions `a < b` of a list of blocks: the merged block replaces position `a`, and position `b` is removed.
nodes.title: Merging two lineage blocks

nodes.summary: The ancestral partitions of the sample along a history, as sets of blocks (forgetting the lineage labels): the ranked labeled history in the sense of Edwards (1970).
nodes.title: Ancestral partitions along a history as sets of blocks
Product of pair counts times a power of two is $n!(n-1)!$
Reindexing the product of pair counts

nodes.summary: Under random joining each history has probability `∏_{k=2}^n C(k, 2)⁻¹`.
nodes.title: Every ranked history is equally likely under random joining

nodes.summary: Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)` under random joining (Edwards 1970; Tajima 1983).
nodes.title: Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)`

nodes.summary: Random joining (Edwards 1970; Kingman 1982): the pair merging at each step is uniform among the current `(n - i).choose 2` pairs and independent of the earlier steps. Kingman (1982) shows that this is the law of the tree topology of the coalescent.
nodes.title: Random joining

nodes.summary: A ranked labeled history of `n` labeled genes, encoded by its coalescence events: at step `i < n - 1` there are `n - i` lineages and the step records the pair that merges (the merged lineage takes the smaller label; the others keep their relative order).
nodes.title: Ranked labeled history

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
